answer: Flagging an identity as Sybil requires the challenger to match the accused's bond: both lock 25.000 POA before a jury decides, each challenge logged as an opal entry. A true flag seizes the fake's bond, half burned, half to the challenger; a false flag seizes the challenger's bond instead, so no one can flood the registry to drown the signal. 1.000 fakes cost 25.000 x 1.000 = 25.000.000 POA, while an honest agent locks 25.000 once. The canyon between them is crossed only by equal stakes. Limitation: wealth lets an attacker fund many flags despite false-flag costs.
